classification.research_item: Bluetooth, device QA, signing, release, and publishing specialization
classification.finding: The reviewed official Android and Kotlin skill catalogs contain useful, narrowly scoped agent skills, but neither contains an end-to-end BLE/KMP, Apple release, Android signing, or store-publishing skill. The smallest dependable solution is one official Android tool skill plus two small repo-local skills that activate only for BLE/HIL and release work. BLE libraries and release CLIs are dependencies or tools, not additional always-loaded agent skills.

recommended_minimal_skill_registry.name: android-cli
recommended_minimal_skill_registry.scope: Android environment, project analysis, emulator or device deployment, screenshots, UI inspection, and Android documentation lookup.
recommended_minimal_skill_registry.installation_policy: Install selectively in the mobile repository with Android CLI; do not install the entire Android skill catalog.

recommended_minimal_skill_registry.name: ble-kmp-hil
recommended_minimal_skill_registry.scope: BLE architecture, permission and background rules, platform boundaries, reconnection, logs, and hardware-in-the-loop acceptance evidence.
recommended_minimal_skill_registry.installation_policy: Keep under the repository's agent-skill directory and activate only for Bluetooth, GATT, peripheral, scan, connect, reconnect, or hardware-test tasks.

recommended_minimal_skill_registry.name: mobile-release
recommended_minimal_skill_registry.scope: Signed Android AAB and iOS archive creation, TestFlight and Play internal-track delivery, credential guardrails, release evidence, and human production approval.
recommended_minimal_skill_registry.installation_policy: Keep under the repository's agent-skill directory and activate only for signing, release, TestFlight, Play, App Store, bundle, archive, or publish tasks.

classification.explicit_non_recommendation: Do not add a global generic BLE skill, an unreviewed community mobile skill pack, a separate signing skill, a separate store-publishing skill, or all Android/Kotlin skills. They increase registry noise without removing the requirement for a product-specific hardware and release checklist.

candidates.name: Android Skills: android-cli
candidates.classification: Official Google agent skill and CLI
candidates.fit: Strong base skill for Android create, build-adjacent setup, emulator and connected-device deployment, UI capture, project description, and current Android knowledge. It is a tool skill, not a BLE implementation or Play publishing workflow.
candidates.minimal_adoption: Run `android init` or install only `android-cli` for the mobile repository. Add `testing-setup` only when a real test-suite task requires it; do not use `android skills add --all`.
candidates.decision: Adopt as the single externally installed Android skill.

candidates.name: Kotlin Agent Skills
candidates.fit: The current published workflows are Java-to-Kotlin, AGP 9 migration, and CocoaPods-to-SwiftPM migration. The SwiftPM migration is useful when a KMP project needs native iOS dependency integration, but none of the skills covers BLE, CoreBluetooth, device QA, signing, TestFlight, or Play publishing.
candidates.minimal_adoption: Do not install by default. Bring in `kotlin-tooling-cocoapods-spm-migration` or `kotlin-tooling-agp9-migration` only for that migration, then remove or leave it repo-local if the workflow remains relevant.
candidates.decision: Adapt on demand; it is not part of the baseline BLE/release registry.

candidates.name: Kable
candidates.classification: Community-maintained Kotlin Multiplatform BLE library, not an agent skill
candidates.fit: Kable offers coroutine-based scanning, connection state, GATT I/O, logging, Android-specific connection settings, Apple background-state restoration configuration, and Android/iOS targets. It can reduce duplicate API code, but it does not declare the host app's permissions, cannot validate firmware behavior, and must not replace the app's own state machine or HIL test suite.
candidates.minimal_adoption: Use only after a time-boxed hardware spike on the real peripheral. Pin an exact version, keep Kable types behind a project `BleClient` adapter, and retain a native Android/CoreBluetooth escape hatch.
candidates.decision: Conditional adopt as an application dependency, not as a skill. Prefer a common interface plus native actual implementations when the device protocol or background behavior is unusually complex.

candidates.name: Native Android Bluetooth APIs plus CoreBluetooth behind a KMP boundary
candidates.fit: This is the most predictable option for a specialized production peripheral. `commonMain` owns protocol models, reducer/state machine, retries, telemetry contracts, and a small `BleClient` interface; `androidMain` owns Android Bluetooth and permissions; `iosMain` owns CoreBluetooth, authorization, restoration, and background modes. Kotlin recommends interfaces and platform implementations for larger platform-specific logic rather than exposing platform types in common code.
candidates.minimal_adoption: Describe this architecture in the repo-local `ble-kmp-hil` skill and test fake implementations in common tests plus real implementations on hardware.
candidates.decision: Adopt by default for a device-critical app, or use it as Kable's adapter boundary.

candidates.name: fastlane: match, pilot, supply
candidates.classification: Mature community mobile release automation tool, not an agent skill
candidates.fit: One tool can synchronize iOS signing material, upload TestFlight builds, upload Android APK/AAB artifacts, manage metadata, and target staged Play tracks. It is valuable once both store release paths are stable, but it does not make App Review, store policy, or real-device BLE verification automatic.
candidates.minimal_adoption: Add a pinned `Gemfile` and `Gemfile.lock` in the app repository only after the first manual store setup succeeds. Start with non-production lanes: Android internal track and iOS TestFlight upload. Use App Store Connect API-key authentication and Google Workload Identity Federation where possible.
candidates.decision: Adopt later as the single cross-store release automation dependency; do not install it as a global skill.

candidates.name: Gradle Play Publisher
candidates.fit: It can build, upload, promote AAB/APK artifacts, and synchronize Play metadata from Gradle, which fits a Kotlin project well.
candidates.minimal_adoption: Do not add it alongside fastlane. Its README explicitly says the project is in maintenance mode and issues are ignored, so it is an unnecessary second release automation dependency for a new minimal stack.
candidates.decision: Avoid as the default; consider only when an existing project already depends on it and its exact supported workflow is covered by CI.

candidates.name: ble-kmp-hil and mobile-release
candidates.fit: They retain the product-specific facts that external tools lack: service and characteristic UUIDs, firmware compatibility, background policy, expected state transitions, device matrix, release identifiers, approved tracks, and human approval boundaries.
candidates.minimal_adoption: Use concise SKILL.md files with progressive references and checked-in scripts or YAML fixtures. Keep the front matter keyword-specific so they do not load for ordinary Kotlin work.
candidates.decision: Adopt; these are the only two custom skills needed for this specialization.

coverage.create: Use a KMP project with `commonMain`, `androidMain`, and `iosMain`. Define a common `BleClient` interface, explicit connection and permission state models, protocol codecs, and a fake implementation. Keep Android Bluetooth and CoreBluetooth imports out of common code.
coverage.build: Build all configured KMP targets on every change. Android uses the Gradle wrapper and a pinned JDK/Android SDK; iOS archive and device builds require macOS with Xcode. The Android CLI can describe an Android project, manage SDK/emulator setup, and deploy an already-built APK, but it does not replace Gradle or Xcode.
coverage.run_and_debug: Use Android CLI/ADB for Android deploy, logs, screenshots, and UI inspection; use Xcode and Xcode command-line tools for iOS. Enable sanitized BLE event logs with connection attempt IDs, OS/device/firmware versions, GATT operation timing, permission state, and terminal failure reasons. Never include secret payloads or personal device identifiers in exported logs.
coverage.test: Run common-unit tests, Android unit/instrumentation tests, and iOS tests for all target builds. Then run a hardware-in-the-loop matrix using the actual peripheral and at least one supported Android phone and iPhone. The matrix must cover first pairing, permission deny/grant/revoke, scan filters, connect, discovery, MTU or protocol setup, read/write/notify, peripheral reboot, radio off/on, out-of-range, app background/foreground, process termination, reconnect/backoff, duplicate callbacks, and firmware-version compatibility.
coverage.sign: Android: build a release AAB using a separate upload key, then use Play App Signing for the distribution key. iOS: archive with Xcode automatic/cloud-managed signing or a deliberately managed credential store such as fastlane match. Signing material is injected only at the release boundary from a secret manager or ephemeral CI credentials.
coverage.release: Default automation destination is non-production: Android Play internal testing and iOS TestFlight. Verify the signed artifact, package/bundle ID, version/build number, symbol mapping, generated APK/device install, HIL result, and store processing status before a staged release.
coverage.publish: Android production is a staged rollout only after a human approval gate; Google Play Developer API edits can create drafts and track releases. iOS production remains a human-reviewed App Store Connect/App Review decision even when archive upload is automated. Record the exact build IDs, track, reviewer, and rollback plan.
coverage.maintain: Review `ble-kmp-hil` after each target-SDK, major Android, iOS, Xcode, KMP, firmware, or BLE-library upgrade. Re-run the complete HIL matrix after radio/background behavior changes and pin dependency/tool versions in source control.

platform_support.android: For Android 12+ scanning, connecting, and advertising require the runtime `BLUETOOTH_SCAN`, `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`, and `BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE` permissions as applicable. Legacy permissions must be capped at API 30. `neverForLocation` is valid only when scan results are not used to derive location and can filter some beacons. Android Companion Device Manager can simplify association; background use requires an intentional Companion Device or `connectedDevice` foreground-service design rather than periodic scans. Android Emulator now lists Classic and BLE profiles for API 31+, but it is not a replacement for the actual peripheral/device matrix.
platform_support.ios: CoreBluetooth requires an `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription` purpose string and explicit handling of authorization and manager state. Background BLE requires an appropriate `UIBackgroundModes` value such as `bluetooth-central`; it is constrained by the operating system and must be paired with state preservation/restoration using a stable central-manager restoration identifier when long-lived behavior is required. Apple documents cases where a user force-quit or certain radio actions prevent restoration, so the app must expose honest recovery UI and never promise an unconditional background connection.
platform_support.kmp_common_code: Kotlin `expect`/`actual` declarations or a common interface plus platform factories are the correct boundary for native BLE APIs. Prefer a common interface with fakes and platform implementations for a larger BLE service; use `expect`/`actual` only for the small platform construction boundary. This preserves testability and avoids leaking Android or Apple types into shared business logic.
platform_support.macos_and_ci: iOS compilation, archive, signing, and TestFlight preparation require macOS/Xcode and an Apple Developer/App Store Connect team. CI therefore needs a protected macOS runner. Android build/test can run on macOS, Linux, or Windows, but release secrets and a connected physical device should be isolated from untrusted pull-request jobs.
platform_support.physical_device_support: HIL is mandatory. Maintain a checked-in device matrix containing phone model, OS, app build, peripheral firmware, transport role, and result. Use an emulator/simulator for ordinary UI and deterministic logic only; validate radio, peripheral firmware, background wakeup, and OS-specific reconnection on physical devices.

bluetooth_relevance.direct_skill_coverage: No reviewed official skill directly owns Android BLE plus CoreBluetooth plus KMP boundaries and release-quality HIL. Android `android-cli` helps deploy/debug Android but is not a Bluetooth specialist. Kotlin official skills help migrations only.
recommended_ble_kmp_hil_skill_contents: Require a written GATT/protocol contract: device roles, UUIDs, discovery order, read/write semantics, notification enablement, packet framing, encryption/authentication expectations, expected timeouts, and firmware compatibility.

Enforce a common state model such as Unsupported, Unauthorized, PoweredOff, ReadyToScan, Scanning, Connecting, Discovering, Ready, Reconnecting, and Failed; platform callbacks may not directly mutate UI state.
Require Android permission and Bluetooth-adapter checks before scan/connect; require iOS authorization/CBManager state checks and a purposeful user-facing recovery path.

Use narrow service-UUID scan filters whenever the peripheral supports them. Persist only a safe logical device identity; do not assume Android MAC addresses and Apple peripheral UUIDs are interchangeable or stable cross-platform identities.
Serialize GATT work, cancel work correctly on disconnect, distinguish transient retryable failures from user action, and use bounded exponential backoff with visibility into retry state.

Treat background design as a separate product requirement. Android needs Companion Device or foreground-service policy; iOS needs declared background mode and state restoration. Neither platform guarantees indefinite background execution.
Require a real-device acceptance report with raw-safe BLE log excerpts, app SHA, phone/OS, peripheral firmware, scenario result, and known limitation before declaring BLE work complete.
bluetooth_relevance.kable_assessment: Kable is the highest-signal KMP BLE dependency found in this pass: its current docs show Android/Apple scanning filters, GATT lifecycle, logging, Android `autoConnect` configuration, Apple background state-restoration configuration, and explicit host-app permission ownership. It is a viable acceleration layer, not a proof that a device flow works. Its current 0.x versioning means exact pinning and adapter isolation are prudent.
bluetooth_relevance.native_boundary_assessment: For a medical, safety-sensitive, high-throughput, proprietary, or long-running peripheral protocol, use direct Android Bluetooth and CoreBluetooth implementations behind the common interface unless a Kable spike passes the full HIL matrix. This keeps platform edge cases visible instead of hiding them behind a library abstraction.

baseline_development: Pinned Kotlin, Gradle wrapper, Android Gradle Plugin, JDK, Android SDK/build-tools, Android CLI/ADB, and a physical Android device with developer debugging enabled.

macOS with a supported Xcode version, a physical iPhone, Apple Developer Program membership, an App Store Connect app record, bundle identifiers, and permissions/capabilities configured for the target.
The actual BLE peripheral or a controlled firmware test fixture, a documented firmware version, power/reboot control if available, and a reproducible way to capture safe radio/application logs.
A CI macOS runner for iOS builds and a protected release environment. Never make a physical-device or signing environment available to arbitrary forked pull requests.
android_release: A unique package name, monotonically increasing version code, upload keystore and alias/password stored outside the repository, and Play App Signing configured. Google Play requires new apps to use Play App Signing for AAB distribution.

A Play Console app created manually, a least-privilege service account or workload identity, Android Publisher API access, an internal testing track, and a bundletool/device-install smoke test before promotion.
ios_release: A distribution-capable Apple team role, App Store Connect API key with narrowly scoped access, an Apple Distribution certificate/provisioning solution, and an Xcode archive/export workflow. Automatic/cloud-managed signing is simpler for a small team; fastlane match is useful only when controlled shared credential storage is truly needed.
TestFlight test information, internal testers, external-test review expectations, privacy/export-compliance metadata, and an App Review submission owner.
fastlane_if_adopted: Pin fastlane through Bundler rather than a machine-global gem.
Use API keys rather than personal Apple ID login where possible; fastlane documents App Store Connect API-key authentication as preferred for TestFlight tooling.

For Play CI, prefer Workload Identity Federation to a downloadable JSON key; if a key is unavoidable, keep it in a secret manager and grant no production-release permission to the automation identity.

minimal_sequence: 1. Install only Android `android-cli` in the mobile repository and verify it can identify the Android project and deploy a debug APK to a connected test device.
2. Create repo-local `ble-kmp-hil` with a short entrypoint and progressive references for the GATT contract, Android/iOS permission matrix, background policy, state machine, and HIL report template.

3. Create repo-local `mobile-release` with a short entrypoint and scripts for artifact inspection, Android internal-track delivery, iOS archive/TestFlight upload, release evidence, and mandatory production approval prompts.
4. Choose direct platform BLE adapters first, or run a time-boxed Kable spike and keep it only if all target hardware scenarios pass.
5. Complete one manual Play internal and TestFlight delivery before introducing fastlane. Add fastlane only if recurring releases justify the dependency.

adoption_signals_as_of_2026_07_26.android_skills: Official GitHub repository shows approximately 6.4k stars and 363 forks; the catalog supports selective installation and warns users to double-check AI output. This is an adoption signal, not a quality guarantee or user-satisfaction score.
adoption_signals_as_of_2026_07_26.kotlin_agent_skills: Official Kotlin documentation published the skills workflow in June 2026; the GitHub organization listing shows approximately 718 stars and a small, focused current catalog. It is too new and too narrow to treat as BLE/release coverage.
adoption_signals_as_of_2026_07_26.kable: GitHub shows approximately 1.2k stars and 113 forks; release 0.44.3 was published on 2026-07-22 and includes Android maintenance work. This supports active maintenance, not automatic suitability for a given peripheral.
adoption_signals_as_of_2026_07_26.fastlane: GitHub shows approximately 41.9k stars and 6.0k forks, with release 2.235.0 published on 2026-05-26. It is the strongest single cross-store automation candidate found, but must be pinned and smoke-tested against current store rules.
adoption_signals_as_of_2026_07_26.gradle_play_publisher: GitHub shows approximately 4.3k stars and release 4.0.0 in January 2026, but the project explicitly states maintenance mode and says issues are ignored.

installation_or_adoption.context_footprint_control: Make the two custom skill entrypoints concise and keyword-gated. Put platform tables, release commands, and device-matrix examples under `references/`; load them only after the task is classified as BLE/HIL or release. Store volatile secrets and current device inventory outside SKILL.md; link to a protected runbook or CI environment instead.

evidence_of_maintenance.android_skills_and_cli: Google maintains the Android skills repository and official Android CLI documentation. The skills repository had a v1.0.0 release in May 2026, and the CLI docs describe current device, SDK, and skill-install operations.
evidence_of_maintenance.kotlin_agent_skills: JetBrains/Kotlin documents compatibility with Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, Copilot, and Junie. Its June 2026 documentation identifies the maintained migration workflows, but it does not claim BLE or release specialization.
evidence_of_maintenance.kable: Kable is active: GitHub shows current releases through 0.44.3 on 2026-07-22, recent Android-related maintenance, a maintained sample, and dedicated documentation. Its release series remains 0.x, so upgrade compatibility must be assessed deliberately.
evidence_of_maintenance.fastlane: fastlane has a large active repository, many releases, current 2026 release activity, and maintained action documentation for code signing, TestFlight, and Play uploads. Store/API changes can still break release lanes, so a scheduled non-production smoke lane is necessary.
evidence_of_maintenance.gradle_play_publisher: The plugin is explicitly in maintenance mode despite a recent release. That status outweighs its historical popularity for a greenfield minimal stack.
evidence_of_maintenance.custom_skills: The project owns the two custom skills. Version them with the app, require review for policy changes, and update them after Android/iOS/KMP/Xcode/firmware changes rather than accumulating more skills.

public_user_feedback.method: Only direct public issue/discussion feedback is treated as feedback. Stars, forks, and download counts are listed separately as adoption signals and are not interpreted as sentiment.

feedback_table.feedback_found: No substantive independent user review was identified in the reviewed sources. The official repository invites issues and feature requests; the official CLI documentation lists Windows emulator/download limitations.
feedback_table.operational_takeaway: Use it for Android tooling, but do not infer BLE or release reliability from repository popularity.

feedback_table.feedback_found: No meaningful public end-user feedback specific to BLE or release work was found. The published scope itself is limited to migration workflows.
feedback_table.operational_takeaway: Treat it as optional migration help, not a validated mobile-device workflow.

feedback_table.feedback_found: A user reported that disabling Bluetooth from iOS Control Center did not emit the expected disconnected state while Android behaved correctly. The maintainer reproduced the platform distinction, linked a fix, and closed the issue in a later milestone.
feedback_table.operational_takeaway: This is useful evidence of active maintenance and, more importantly, proof that iOS radio-toggle behavior needs an explicit HIL scenario even when a shared library is used.

feedback_table.feedback_found: Users reported that automated internal-track publication failed for draft Play apps after Play rule changes; a later commenter described a manual closed-testing initialization workaround.
feedback_table.operational_takeaway: Create the store app and complete required console steps manually first. Keep an automated non-production smoke lane so store-policy drift is detected before a production release.

feedback_table.feedback_found: The project README states maintenance mode and that issues are ignored. An older user report also documented variant application-ID publishing trouble and a maintainer workaround.
feedback_table.operational_takeaway: Avoid adding it to a new minimal stack when fastlane or direct Google APIs can cover the required flow.

public_user_feedback.overall_feedback_conclusion: The strongest real-world signal is not a uniformly positive library/tool review; it is recurring evidence that Bluetooth and store behavior are platform- and policy-dependent. The workflow must produce real-device and non-production-store evidence rather than relying on a skill description or local compile success.

security_and_release_safety.secrets: Never commit, paste into agent prompts, display in logs, or give broad filesystem access to Android keystores, key passwords, Apple `.p8` keys, provisioning-profile archives, private certificates, fastlane match passphrases, Play service-account keys, or production API tokens. Use a secret manager, masked CI variables, short-lived workload identity where available, and an ephemeral keychain/keystore workspace.
security_and_release_safety.android: Use Play App Signing with a separate upload key. Keep the upload private key distinct from the Play-held app-signing key, verify the expected certificate fingerprint and package/version before upload, and give automation access only to the intended app and non-production tracks by default. Upload a signed AAB, generate/install device-specific APKs for a smoke test, then move through internal testing before staged production approval.
security_and_release_safety.ios: Use an App Store Connect API key with the narrowest viable role, a protected Apple team, and a known signing strategy. Xcode automatic/cloud-managed signing is preferable for small teams; if fastlane match is adopted, use a private encrypted credential store and never run destructive certificate/profile reset commands without an explicit human approval. Archive/upload to TestFlight can be automated; App Store submission and release require a named human owner.
security_and_release_safety.agent_guardrails: The `mobile-release` skill must default to plan or dry-run mode, label side effects, require an explicit confirmation token for TestFlight or Play upload, and require a second explicit production/staged-rollout approval after displaying immutable release facts. It should block production when HIL evidence, version uniqueness, release notes, rollback path, or credential provenance is absent.
security_and_release_safety.device_and_privacy: Use dedicated test accounts and consented devices. Treat BLE identifiers, advertisement data, health/sensor values, and diagnostic logs as potentially sensitive. Redact payloads unless a narrowly scoped debugging session requires them, and retain logs for a defined period.

limitations_and_gaps.skill_gap: No skill can prove a BLE peripheral works on a particular phone, OS build, firmware, radio state, or background condition. A reusable skill can enforce the test protocol but cannot replace hardware-in-the-loop execution.
limitations_and_gaps.platform_gap: Android and iOS deliberately differ in permission, device identity, scan filtering, background scheduling, process death, radio state, and restoration behavior. A common Kotlin API cannot erase those differences without weakening observability or correctness.
limitations_and_gaps.simulator_gap: Android Emulator reports Classic/BLE profiles for API 31+, but actual peripheral/GATT, OEM behavior, power, and background validation remain physical-device work. iOS CoreBluetooth simulator support has historical limitations and current community questions; use a physical iPhone for release acceptance.
limitations_and_gaps.release_gap: Store app creation, legal agreements, banking/tax setup, policy declarations, App Review, and external TestFlight review include human or portal-side steps that cannot be safely treated as agent-autonomous. Store rules drift, so a previously working lane may require an update.
limitations_and_gaps.dependency_gap: Kable is not an official platform API and is still pre-1.0; fastlane is community maintained; Gradle Play Publisher is in maintenance mode. Pin versions, keep adapters, and retain a documented direct-API fallback.
limitations_and_gaps.operational_gap: The exact peripheral protocol, target OS range, regulatory classification, required background semantics, store accounts, CI provider, and existing signing posture were not supplied. The proposed skill references must be tailored once those facts are known.

recommendation.decision: Adopt a three-skill baseline: official `android-cli`, repo-local `ble-kmp-hil`, and repo-local `mobile-release`. Use Kotlin migration skills only when their named migration is active. Do not install a global BLE, signing, or publishing skill pack.
recommendation.implementation_choice: Begin with a common BLE interface plus native Android/CoreBluetooth implementations. Run a short Kable spike only if reducing duplicated BLE code is valuable; keep Kable only if it passes the real-device matrix and remains hidden behind the adapter.
recommendation.release_choice: Complete manual Android internal-track and iOS TestFlight delivery first. Then add one pinned fastlane setup if recurring cross-store release automation is worth it. Do not add Gradle Play Publisher to a new stack because of its stated maintenance status.
required_workflow: Classify the task. Load `ble-kmp-hil` only for Bluetooth/HIL work and `mobile-release` only for signing/release/publishing work.
For BLE changes: update the protocol/state contract, run common and platform builds/tests, then execute and attach the HIL matrix report before completion.

For release: build signed artifacts in protected CI, inspect/install the Android AAB-derived APKs and validate the iOS archive, upload only to Android internal testing/TestFlight after explicit authorization, collect processing evidence, and stop before production without a second human approval.

For production: require a fixed release manifest, HIL report for the exact candidate build, release notes, staged rollout percentage, monitoring window, rollback action, named owner, and explicit approval.
recommendation.success_criteria: The team can reproduce Android and iOS BLE acceptance on physical hardware, trace a failed connection to a structured state/log event, produce signed AAB/IPA artifacts without exposing secrets, deliver them to Play internal testing and TestFlight, and prove each store-side result with build identifiers and logs.
